newsitem.title: UK: India train joins long list of political attacks. [CORRECTED 22:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: India train joins long list of political attacks. [CORRECTED 22:45 GMT]

text.p: The bomb aboard a train in India's northeastern (corrects from "northwestern") Assam state, in which at least 300 people were reported killed on Monday, was the latest in a series of violent political incidents during 1996.
Following is a chronology of some of the major incidents in which political violence was suspected or established:
Jan 31 - In Sri Lanka, up to 90 people die after a truck bomb explodes in the centre of Colombo when a suicide bomber rams the Central Bank.
Feb 9 - Huge bomb rocks London's Docklands area, killing two and injuring 100. Irish Republican Army (IRA) claims responsibility, ending 17-month ceasefire with Britain.
Feb 18 - Suspected IRA bomber blows himself up with own bomb on bus in central London's -- one dead, nine wounded.
Feb 25 - Islamic Hamas suicide bomber blows up bus near Jerusalem's central bus station. Twenty-six people die in this attack and second assault in southern town of Ashkelon.
March 3 - Another Hamas bus bomb in Jerusalem kills 18 people and the suicide bomber.
March 4 - Moslem suicide bomber kills 12 people outside crowded mall in Israeli city of Tel Aviv.
June 11 - Bomb explodes on the Moscow underground, killing four people and injuring 12.
June 15 - IRA car bomb explodes at Manchester shopping mall during European soccer championship injuring more than 200.
June 25 - Fuel truck bomb kills 19 American soldiers and wounds nearly 400 people at a U.S. military complex in Khobar near the Saudi Arabian oil city of Dhahran.
July 14 - Suspected Republican guerrillas bomb hotel at Enniskillen, Northern Ireland, injured 17. IRA denies responsibility.

July 17 - Paris-bound TWA flight 800 explodes in a fireball off New York coast, killing all 230 aboard Boeing 747. Although a bomb is first suspected, later investigation points to explosion being caused by technical failure.
July 20 - Basque separatist group ETA bombs Reus airport in northeastern Spain, injuring 35 people.
July 22 - Bomb blast at Pakistan's Lahore Airport kills at least four people and injures about 70.
July 24 - Two bombs rip through crowded commuter train in Colombo, killing at least 78 and injuring more than 450.
July 27 - Bomb explosion rocks Centennial park in the Olympic city of Atlanta, killing two and wounding 110.
Aug 27 - Armed Iraqis hijack a Sudanese Airbus 310 to London's Stansted airport where they release 199 passengers and crew and are taken into police custody.
Sept 23 - Four gunmen attack a Sunni Moslem mosque in the Pakistani city of Multan, killing at least 21 people.
Oct 7 - IRA bombs Britain's army headquarters in Northern Ireland, injuring 31 people, one of whom dies of his wounds on Oct 11.
Nov 10 - Thirteen people are killed when bomb blasts a crowd of mourners at a Moscow cemetery.
Nov 15 - Indian left-wing extremists kill 13 policemen and one civilian in a rocket attack on Sirpuru village in southern Andhra Pradesh state.
Nov 23 - Hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 crashes into the sea off the Comoro Islands, killing 125.
Dec 3 - Four people die and more than 90 are injured when a explosion rocks an underground station in Paris.
Dec 17 - Peruvian rebels storm the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima, threatening to kill almost 490 hostages unless the government freed jailed comrades; many of the hostages subsequently freed.
Dec 30 - Bomb devastates packed train in northeast (corrects from "northwest") Indian state of Assam, killing at least 300. Police blame Bodo separatist militants.
